figures.cap: triangle PQR with QR=12, PR=20, angle Q=120 degrees, angle P = x degrees

parts.latex:
Which calculation should be used to find the value of $x$ in $\triangle PQR$ ?

\exfigure{2843_q3a_1}

solutions.latex:
Two angles and their opposite sides are involved, so use the sine rule. The side opposite $x^\circ$ is 12 and the side opposite $120^\circ$ is 20.
$$\dfrac{\sin x^\circ}{12} = \dfrac{\sin 120^\circ}{20}$$
Hence the answer is option B.

2843_q3a_1.notes: Triangle PQR with 12, 20, 120° and x° placed as in the crop, in the house font. No angle arcs, matching the crop. Rules 1, 11.

figures.cap: triangle ABC with angles 87 and 47 and BC = 230 m
solution sketch: Triangle with angle B = 46 degrees marked

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{3296_q7b_s1}

Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ABC &= 180^\circ-87^\circ-47^\circ \\ &= 46^\circ \end{aligned}$$
By the sine rule in triangle ABC:
$$\dfrac{AC}{\sin 46^\circ} = \dfrac{230}{\sin 47^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} AC &= \dfrac{230\sin 46^\circ}{\sin 47^\circ} \\ &\approx 226.22 \text{ m (2 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the correct sine rule equation, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle with sides x m and 5 m and angles 102 and 32 degrees

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 102^\circ} = \dfrac{5}{\sin 32^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{5\sin 102^\circ}{\sin 32^\circ} \\ &\approx 9.2 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = 9.2 \text{ m (2 significant figures)}$$
criteria: Correct substitution and rearrangement, or equivalent merit
Writes the sine rule with correct values, or equivalent merit
